# Pie chart syntax

<!-- Generated by tools/gen-grammar from packages/diagram-pie/grammar/pie.ebnf. Do not edit: run `pnpm gen:grammar`. -->

Pie chart syntax (R-PARSE-9, D54): the normative grammar of `pie` diagrams.

The hand-written parser in `src/parser/` implements it; `tools/gen-grammar` builds a reference
parser, a sentence generator, highlighters and the syntax reference page from it. mermaid@12
decides what is valid, this file is fixed to match, and the parser must match this file
(DESIGN §4.4). mermaid@12 parsed pie with Langium (`pie.langium` and `common.langium` in
`@mermaid-js/parser`); the rules below are its token rules, in its order, and its grammar.

**Lexer input.** The lexer reads the diagram body as mermaid@12 handed it to its lexer: front
matter and `%%{…}%%` directives removed; CRLF and CR read as LF; `="x"` inside an HTML tag read
as `='x'`; `%%` comment lines removed and leading blanks trimmed; on a line with
`style…:…#…;` (or `classDef…`) the last `;` dropped; `#name;` / `#123;` entities read as
opaque text; and a line break appended. Keywords are case-sensitive.

Each section and statement ends at a line break (or the end of the text); `;` is not a
separator.

## Grammar

EBNF: `[ x ]` is optional, `{ x }` repeats zero or more times, `x+` one or more times, `|` separates alternatives. Upper-case names and `subgraph`, `end`, `acc_…`, `direction_…` are tokens (see below). A rule marked `@Type` builds an AST node of that type.

A chart is `pie` (with `showData`), then sections and statements, one per line. The
`YAML`, `DIRECTIVE` and `COMMENT` tokens of the lexer are skipped before parsing.

```ebnf
pie = { NEWLINE } Header { NEWLINE | statement NEWLINE } [ statement ] EOF ;
```

```ebnf
Header @Header = PIE [ SHOW_DATA ] ;
```

```ebnf
statement = Slice
          | Title
          | AccTitle
          | AccDescr ;
```

`"Dogs" : 386`: a section, its label and its value. A repeated label keeps its first
value.

```ebnf
Slice @Slice = STRING COLON NUMBER ;
```

`title Pets adopted`: the title drawn above the chart (the last one wins).

```ebnf
Title @Title = TITLE ;
```

`accTitle: …`: the accessible title.

```ebnf
AccTitle @AccTitle = ACC_TITLE ;
```

`accDescr: …` or `accDescr { … }`: the accessible description.

```ebnf
AccDescr @AccDescr = ACC_DESCR ;
```

## Tokens

The lexer works in modes (`INITIAL` and the ones below). In each mode it tries the rules in this order and takes the first that matches; a rule may push a mode or pop back to the previous one. Rules without a token emit nothing.

Modes: `INITIAL`.

| Modes | Token | Pattern | Action | Doc |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| INITIAL | SHOW_DATA | `showData(?:(?=%%)\|(?!\S))` |  | `pie showData`: the legend shows each value after its label, as `Dogs [386]`. |
| INITIAL | PIE | `pie(?:(?=%%)\|(?!\S))` |  | `pie`: starts a pie chart. `pie showData` shows the values in the legend. |
| INITIAL | COLON | `:` |  |  |
| INITIAL | NUMBER | `-?[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(?!\.)\|-?(?:0\|[1-9][0-9]*)(?!\.)` |  | A section's value: a number such as `42` or `3.5`, never negative; no sign other than `-`, no exponent, no leading zeros and no `.` without digits on both sides. |
| INITIAL | ACC_DESCR | `[\t ]*accDescr(?:[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)\|\s*\{[^}]*\})` |  | `accDescr: …` (the rest of the line) or `accDescr { … }` (over lines, to `}`): the accessible description of the chart. |
| INITIAL | ACC_TITLE | `[\t ]*accTitle[\t ]*:(?:[^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[^\n\r]*)` |  | `accTitle: …`: the accessible title of the chart, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | TITLE | `[\t ]*title(?:[\t ][^\n\r]*?(?=%%)\|[\t ][^\n\r]*\|)` |  | `title …`: the title drawn above the chart, the rest of the line. |
| INITIAL | STRING | `"(?:[^"\\]\|\\.)*"\|'(?:[^'\\]\|\\.)*'` |  | A section's label: `"…"` or `'…'`; `\` escapes the next character, and a label may span lines. |
| INITIAL | NEWLINE | `\r?\n` |  |  |
| INITIAL | — | `[\t ]+` |  |  |
| INITIAL | YAML | `---[\t ]*\r?\n(?:[\S\s]*?\r?\n)?---(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `---` … `---` block inside the body: skipped. |
| INITIAL | DIRECTIVE | `[\t ]*%%\{[\S\s]*?\}%%(?:\r?\n\|(?!\S))` |  | A `%%{…}%%` left in the text the lexer reads: skipped. |
| INITIAL | COMMENT | `[\t ]*%%[^\n\r]*` |  | `%%` to the end of the line, after other text: a comment. |
| INITIAL | EOF | `$` |  | The end of the text. |

Removed before lexing (highlighted only):

- COMMENT: `^[^\S\n]*%%(?!\{)[^\n]+`
- DIRECTIVE: `[^\S\n]*%%\{[\s\S]*?\}%%`
